hypotheses.title: Volume-Weighted 3-Day Liquidity Exhaustion Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Short-term (3-day) price reversals are significantly magnified when accompanied by anomalous liquidity surges (volume relative to its 60-day moving average). By multiplying normalized return change ts_delta(close, 3) / close with the cross-sectional percentile rank of normalized turnover rank(volume / ts_mean(volume, 60)), the signal isolates liquidity-exhausted price overreactions. Smoothing with a 10-day linear decay dampens noise, and subindustry group ranking ensures sector neutrality.
confounders: Sustained fundamental news breaks where high volume signals genuine repricing rather than overreaction
Earnings announcement windows creating extreme directional momentum
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails during aggressive trend-continuation regimes with low cross-sectional dispersion.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain 1-Hop Information Breadth and Operational Resilience
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Supply chain information breadth (pv13_1l_scibr) measures the diversification and network centrality of a firm's direct customer and supplier relationships. Firms with higher informational breadth exhibit greater operational resilience against supplier shocks and demand disruptions. A 20-day ts_backfill ensures continuous coverage for periodic updates, while group_zscore and a 15-day linear decay prevent turnover spikes.
confounders: Restructuring or supplier consolidation reducing breadth without hurting profitability
Data reporting lags in international supplier disclosures
hypotheses.falsification_test: Inverts during macro shocks where complex supply chains experience greater systemic bottlenecks than localized single-supplier firms.

hypotheses.title: Systematic Risk Dispersion and Idiosyncratic Pricing Power
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Systematic risk (systematic_risk_last_90_days, the R^2 of stock returns against broad market and factor benchmarks over 90 days) captures the proportion of variance driven purely by macroeconomic beta rather than firm-specific fundamentals. Stocks with high systematic risk are macro-sensitive price takers, whereas stocks with low systematic risk within the same subindustry possess strong idiosyncratic pricing power and economic moats. Smoothing with a 15-day linear decay creates a robust idiosyncratic quality tilt with low turnover.
confounders: Macro liquidity crises where all stocks correlate to 1.0 regardless of fundamentals
Speculative bull rallies where high-beta commodities outperform
hypotheses.falsification_test: Underperforms during sharp liquidity-driven market rallies led by speculative high-beta equities.
